handoff: Review #1: spec met (AC1–AC7 tested at S1/S3; AC8 needs a person with a real remote); suite 1264 green, typecheck green. Blocking F1: after createIssue succeeds, a failing intake runTick (e.g. tick_locked while watch runs) fails the command and invites a retry that duplicates the issue — return the created story with exit 0 and point at norn sync instead, with an S1 test. Minor F2: intake summary not filtered to the created story. Nit F3: ask() Ctrl-C doc.

findings.title: A failed intake tick after createIssue reports failure and invites a duplicate create
findings.detail:
After `remote.createIssue` succeeds, `runTick(ctx, { sync: "force" })` can throw. The common case is `tick_locked` from `acquireTickLock` (runtime/tick.ts:103) while `norn watch` or a cron tick holds the lock. Observe or act can also fail. The error reaches the person as the command's failure (busy exit, do_instead "wait for it to finish; ticks are idempotent"), so they rerun `norn story create`, and a second identical issue is created. The issue already exists and the next tick of watch takes it in anyway (GR1). Only the report is wrong, and it costs a duplicate on the remote. B22 promises 'retry cleanly' only for failures before the create.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Once the issue exists, never fail the command over intake. Catch a runTick error, return the created story (key and url) with exit 0, and add a note that intake runs on the next tick or with `norn sync` (do_instead `norn sync`, never a re-create). Add an S1 test: hold the tick lock (or make observe throw), run story create, and check exit 0, the key printed, one create call, and a do_instead/note naming `norn sync`.

findings.title: 'took it in' is printed even when this story's intake decision failed
findings.detail:
`intake` collects every intake_story decision of the tick, other stories included, and the markdown always says 'Created … and took it in'. That holds even when the decision for the created story has ok:false, or when no decision exists for it (for example a story that has no label match after config changes).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Filter intake to the created story's key. Say 'took it in' only when its decision is ok; otherwise name the error and `norn sync`.

findings.title: ask() doc says Ctrl-C returns null
findings.detail:
ask() reads in cooked mode, not raw mode, so Ctrl-C raises SIGINT and ends the process; it never returns null. Only Ctrl-D (end of input) returns null.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Say 'null on end of input (Ctrl-D)'.
